connectors.name: Google BigQuery
connectors.description: Google BigQuery serverless data warehouse. Connects, discovers, and reads over the first-class ADBC BigQuery driver; writes land as Parquet load jobs via the BigQuery API (direct media upload, no GCS staging bucket). Authenticates with a service-account JSON key (default) or an OAuth user-credential flow; all connection state is passed via adbc.bigquery.sql.* driver options.

connectors.name: ClickHouse
connectors.description: ClickHouse column-oriented OLAP database. Reads and writes over the async SQLAlchemy clickhouse+asynch transport (the clickhouse-sqlalchemy dialect on the asynch native-protocol driver): username/password authentication, a three-value ssl_mode (disable / require / verify-full) realized through the driver's secure/verify connect arguments, and schema/table/view discovery via ClickHouse's INFORMATION_SCHEMA views. ClickHouse's native protocol has no STARTTLS-style upgrade - TLS is a separate listener (9440) from the plaintext one (9000) - so ssl_mode and port must agree. Write-path facts are declared honestly rather than conveniently: ClickHouse has no MERGE, no ON CONFLICT and no ON DUPLICATE KEY, so merge_form is 'none' and upsert streams are refused at handshake instead of silently duplicating rows (row-collapsing upserts are a table-engine property - ReplacingMergeTree plus FINAL - not a statement grammar the engine can render); DDL is never transactional, so staging uses a real MergeTree table created and dropped outside any transaction. No first-class ADBC driver and no Arrow Flight SQL endpoint exist for ClickHouse, so the SQLAlchemy transport is the only supported path; batches land through the native columnar block insert the driver performs on executemany, which is why bulk_load declares no separate mechanism and why write_unit asks the coalescer for large batches (ClickHouse penalizes small, frequent inserts with part explosion).

connectors.name: DuckDB
connectors.description: DuckDB, an embedded in-process OLAP database. Reads and writes over the synchronous SQLAlchemy duckdb+duckdb_engine transport against a local database file or an in-memory database. DuckDB is not a client-server system: there is no host, port, username, password or TLS handshake, and access is governed by local filesystem permissions - so the connector declares auth type 'none' and no TLS block. Schema/table/view discovery runs against information_schema. The declared SQL write path is stage-then-merge: a session-scoped CREATE TEMPORARY TABLE ... AS SELECT ... WHERE 1 = 0 stage (DuckDB implements no CREATE TABLE ... LIKE), a Postgres-style INSERT ... ON CONFLICT ... DO UPDATE upsert, and transactional DDL, so the whole cycle rolls back as one unit. Batches land through the connector's bulk hook, which registers the Arrow batch on the in-process connection and INSERT ... SELECTs from it - DuckDB's native zero-copy Arrow ingestion - instead of row-by-row executemany.

connectors.name: MariaDB
connectors.description: MariaDB relational database (11.4 LTS), the community-developed fork of MySQL. Reads and writes over the async SQLAlchemy mariadb+aiomysql transport: the mariadb dialect name puts SQLAlchemy in MariaDB-only mode, so the server's 'X.Y.Z-MariaDB' version string is required and MariaDB-specific behaviour is never gated on a MySQL version probe. Username/password authentication, MariaDB's --ssl / --ssl-verify-server-cert TLS surface expressed as a four-value ssl_mode with a post-connect Ssl_cipher enforcement probe, schema/table/view discovery via information_schema, and declared SQL write-path capabilities (stage-then-merge with CREATE TEMPORARY TABLE ... LIKE and INSERT ... ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE). The session is pinned to SET time_zone = '+00:00' so TIMESTAMP values carry a well-defined UTC instant. No ADBC driver and no Arrow Flight SQL endpoint exist for MariaDB, so the SQLAlchemy transport is the only supported path; batches land via executemany (LOAD DATA LOCAL INFILE is not reachable through the engine's connect-argument surface). MariaDB natives with no MySQL counterpart - UUID, INET4 and INET6 - are read as text.

connectors.name: MySQL
connectors.description: MySQL open-source relational database. Connects over the MySQL wire protocol via the async SQLAlchemy mysql+aiomysql dialect for structured data storage, querying, runtime table discovery, and DDL/write-back.

connectors.name: PostgreSQL
connectors.description: PostgreSQL database connector. Reads and writes Arrow data over the first-class ADBC libpq driver (COPY-based bulk ingestion) as the default transport, with an async SQLAlchemy (asyncpg) transport as the engine-side SQL path. Username/password authentication, libpq TLS modes (disable through verify-full), and table/view discovery via information_schema.

connectors.name: Amazon Redshift
connectors.description: Amazon Redshift cloud data warehouse connector using the vendor-supported synchronous SQLAlchemy driver redshift+redshift_connector (Amazon's redshift-connector DBAPI via the sqlalchemy-redshift dialect). Redshift has no first-class ADBC driver and exposes no Arrow Flight SQL endpoint; its native bulk load (COPY) reads only from S3/EMR/DynamoDB/SSH and never from the client connection, so there is no COPY FROM STDIN path to implement and the connector uses the SQLAlchemy transport for connect, DDL, and writes: batched INSERT plus a MERGE-based upsert (Redshift has no ON CONFLICT), with no bulk-load mechanism declared. The engine dispatches the synchronous driver on its sync engine path. Works with both provisioned clusters (host *.redshift.amazonaws.com) and Redshift Serverless (host *.redshift-serverless.amazonaws.com), both on port 5439. Authenticates with a Redshift database username and password. TLS is negotiated through the redshift_connector driver's two connect parameters (ssl + sslmode); the driver documents only the certificate-verification modes verify-ca and verify-full and verifies against its bundled Amazon Trust CA. AWS IAM database authentication and IdP/SSO federation are alternatives to a static username/password but are NOT modeled in this connector version.

connectors.name: Xero
connectors.description: Xero cloud accounting platform. Reads and writes accounting data — invoices, credit notes, contacts, bank transactions, payments, items, accounts, manual journals, the general ledger and organisation settings — via the Xero Accounting API (api.xro/2.0). OAuth 2.0 authorization code with granular accounting scopes and refresh-token rotation; each connection targets exactly one Xero organisation (tenant), selected after authorisation from GET /connections.
